title: Operator Script DSL and CLI Runtime: design & roadmap
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary
This document specifies the design, safety constraints, telemetry contract, and a two-quarter roadmap for a small, opinionated Operator Script DSL and accompanying CLI runtime. The goal is to enable platform operators and SREs to author compact, auditable, and executable operational playbooks (runbooks) that can be validated, simulated, and executed against the platform with minimal risk.

Context and motivation
- Current pain: engineers author free-form runbooks (markdown + ad-hoc scripts). Operators copy/paste and run commands manually; this is error-prone, hard to test, and hard to attribute.
- Desired: a constrained, declarative script model for common operator actions (drain, rebalance, prefetch cohort, model swap, promote-canary, manual-evict, snapshot) plus a CLI that validates, simulates, and executes with RBAC, dry-run, and observability hooks.
- Non-goal: replace full orchestration systems (k8s operators) or business logic embedded in services. This is for human-operated, low-latency corrective actions and routine maintenance.

Principles
1. Safety-first: all scripts are validated against a safety policy before execution. Defaults are pessimistic (fail closed).
2. Idempotency: operations should be re-runnable where possible; DSL encourages idempotent primitives.
3. Auditable: every execution is logged, versioned, and tied to a ticket/incident and an operator identity.
4. Testable & simulatable: a local "simulator" mode mirrors platform state for offline testing.
5. Minimal surface area: DSL primitives are intentionally small and vetted. Extend via approved extension points only.

DSL overview (human-friendly description)
- Format: YAML-first, 1–2 screens per script.
- Top-level fields: metadata, preconditions, steps, postchecks, rollbacks, telemetry.
- Primitives (examples):
  - api_call: call an internal platform API with typed input and explicit timeout
  - shell_safe: run a restricted shell command in a sandboxed operator container
  - schedule_prefetch: request prefetch cohort for model X with cohort_id
  - model_swap: swap runtime model variant on a host/pool with validation window
  - drain_node / undrain_node: soft drain with annotated reason and ETA
  - wait_for_sli: await an SLI condition using timeframe and threshold
  - notify: send structured notification to ops channels (Slack, PagerDuty)
  - approve_gate: require an interactive approve step tied to a ticket id

Example script (YAML)
---
metadata:
  name: "rebalance-small-prefetch-cohort"
  owner: "platform-operator-team"
  ticket: "INC-4321"
preconditions:
  - cluster-health: "green"
  - s3-access: "has_key"
steps:
  - schedule_prefetch:
      model: "redwood/llama-13b-q8"
      cohort_id: "cohort-202611"
      expected_size: 40
  - wait_for_sli:
      sli: "prefetch-complete"
      window: "10m"
postchecks:
  - query-prefetch-status: "cohort-202611"
  - assert: "complete == true"
rollback:
  - api_call:
      endpoint: "/prefetch/cancel"
      body: {cohort_id: "cohort-202611"}
telemetry:
  runbook_id: "prf-2026-11"
  emit: ["prefetch.requested", "prefetch.completed"]
---

Execution model and CLI behaviors
- validate: runbook-cli validate <file> -> schema check + static analysis + safety policy check
- simulate: runbook-cli simulate <file> --state snapshot.json -> executes in simulator, emits synthetic telemetry and cost estimates
- dry-run: runbook-cli execute <file> --dry-run -> runs prechecks and prints planned API calls without changes
- execute: runbook-cli execute <file> --ticket INC-4321 -> runs with RBAC, interactive approve gates prompt, logs to operator-audit
- guardrails: operations are rate-limited, concurrency-limited, and may require multi-approver for high-impact changes

Safety policy (summary)
- Thresholds requiring multi-approver:
  - any operation affecting > 20% of a tenant's capacity
  - model-swap to a non-verified variant
  - cluster-wide drains
- Time windows: destructive operations are not allowed during blackout windows (nightly commit window 02:00–05:00 UTC unless emergency)
- Immutable audit fields: metadata.owner, metadata.ticket enforced at validation time

Telemetry contract (what the runtime emits)
- runbook.execution.start {runbook_id, operator_id, ticket, mode}
- runbook.step.start {runbook_id, step_index, primitive, inputs}
- runbook.step.end {runbook_id, step_index, status, duration_ms, result_codes}
- runbook.execution.end {runbook_id, status, duration_ms, total_cost_estimate}
- runbook.simulation.report {runbook_id, checks, estimated_telemetry}
- Error taxonomy: validation_error, safety_block, runtime_error, external_api_error

Observability & dashboarding requirements (minimum)
- Build a "Runbook Execution" dashboard with the following panels:
  - Recent executions table (last 7d) with runbook_id, operator, ticket, status, duration
  - Failure heatmap by primitive type (api_call, model_swap, drain_node)
  - Average time-to-complete for common runbooks (prefetch, rebalance)
  - Safety policy blocks over time (count and top blocking rules)
- Alerts:
  - runbook.execution.failure.rate > 5% for a given runbook in 1h -> pager to platform-operator oncall
  - simulation vs execution divergence > 20% (estimated vs actual cost/time) -> create investigation ticket

Operator UX and CLI ergonomics
- Default to interactive mode with compact progress spinner and context lines for failures
- Provide auto-generated human-readable changelog for each runbook execution
- Support auto-complete for primitives and recommended argument values via CLI plugin (bash/zsh/fish)
- CLI must include a "why-blocked" explainer that surfaces the safety rule and suggested remediation

Rollout plan (milestones)
Quarter A (Q1 2027) - prototype & internal pilot
  - implement YAML schema, validator, and simulator (local-only)
  - implement 6 vetted primitives: api_call, wait_for_sli, schedule_prefetch, model_swap, drain_node, notify
  - integrate audit logging to operator-audit service
  - internal pilot with one operator pod group (platform-core)
Quarter B (Q2 2027) - hardened runtime & observability
  - RBAC enforcement and multi-approver flows
  - telemetry contract implemented and dashboard panels created
  - cost-estimation module and simulation divergence alert
  - operator training + playbook migration clinic

Migration & backward-compatibility strategy
- Provide a migration helper that converts canonical markdown runbooks to the DSL where possible.
- Maintain a compatibility shim for legacy scripts executed via a sandboxed runner; mark those runs with label legacy_runner.

Testing & verification matrix
- Unit: schema and primitive unit tests (owner: eng-platform-infra)
- Integration: simulator vs staging platform (owner: eng-serving-runtime)
- Chaos tests: intentionally fail API endpoints during simulate to validate rollbacks (owner: eng-sre)
- Safety fuzzing: randomized scripts run against simulator with safety policy enforced (owner: reliability lab)

Open risks & mitigations
- Risk: operators over-rely on simulation and skip live safety checks -> Mitigation: enforce safety checks at runtime and add a mandatory post-execution verification step tied to ticket closure.
- Risk: misplaced trust in cost estimates -> Mitigation: conservative defaults, require opt-in for any runbook that estimates > $500 estimated cost.
- Risk: DSL proliferation/duplication -> Mitigation: runbook registry + required review for new runbook entries; quarterly registry pruning.

Ownership & contacts
- Product owner: Priya Raman (platform-product)
- Engineering lead: Maya Chen (eng-platform)
- Observability: Diego Alvarez (eng-platform-observability)
- SRE safety review: Ethan Cole (eng-sre)

Appendix: sample validator CLI output (stylized)
$ runbook-cli validate rebalance.yaml
✔ schema: OK
✖ safety: BLOCKED -> rule: "cluster-wide drains require 2 approvers"
  reason: affects 32% of tenant capacity
  suggestion: reduce target scope or request multi-approver flag (--approvers 2)

Appendix: minimal YAML schema excerpt
- metadata.name: string (required)
- metadata.owner: string (required)
- preconditions: list of precondition objects
- steps: ordered list of primitives (mapping of primitive name -> args)
- rollback: ordered list
- telemetry: runbook_id, emit list

Next steps (immediate)
- Approve the safety policy draft (owners: eng-sre, security)
- Allocate 3 FTEs (1 infra, 1 observability, 1 SRE) to Q1 prototype
- Schedule pilot week with platform-core operators (target date: 2027-02-14)

This document should be treated as a living specification. Feedback and suggested changes should be submitted as PRs against the runbook-dsl repo and new reviewers added to the reviewers list above.
